title: Deferred Interest on Crestline Credit Card Promotional Purchases: Accrual and When It May Be Assessed
content:
On a Crestline Credit Card deferred-interest plan, interest accrues from the purchase date at the account's purchase APR on the plan's remaining balance and is shown on each statement as an accrual; it is not charged while the plan runs.

## When accrued interest may be assessed

**Accrued interest may be assessed only after the promotional period counted from the promotional purchase has ended.** The plan period is the plan's length in months counted from the promotional purchase. Months are counted as calendar months from the anchor date to the same day of the month, falling back to the last day of that month when that day does not exist.

- **Clock starts:** the promotional purchase, as its posting date on the card ledger shows it.
- **Counting:** the purchase posting date plus the plan's length in calendar months, to the same day of the month (or the last day of that month).
- **Comparison:** an assessment is not earlier than that date; the date itself qualifies.

| Hypothetical 6-month plan, purchase posted 15 March | May accrued interest be assessed? |
|---|---|
| on 14 September (the plan's expiration date, the day before the counted date) | no |
| on 15 September (the counted date) | yes |
| any later day | yes |

Purchase posted 31 August with a 6-month plan, in a year whose following February has 28 days: the counted date falls back to 28 February, and an assessment may be made from 28 February.

## Assessment clause — no longer in force

The deferred-interest rule formerly stated that when the plan's remaining balance is above 0.00 at the end of its expiration date, all interest accrued since the purchase date is assessed in one entry at the next statement closing and the unpaid balance becomes a standard balance. **That clause is no longer in force; it is superseded by the current basis for assessing deferred interest.**

## Clauses in force

- When the balance is paid in full by the plan's expiration date, nothing is assessed and the accruals lapse.
- A merchandise credit on the ticket reduces the remaining balance but never reverses an accrual already recorded.
- Equal-payment plans have no deferred interest.
